absent: Matching and iteration rules inside core grouping lookup helpers beyond membership and throttling exclusion.
Transfer mechanics of queued task movement and rescheduling notification beyond requesting a fresh selection.
Definitions of task blocking, deactivation and attachment helpers and their queue and clock effects.
Full run queue and task structure layouts beyond fields referenced in these fragments.
Scheduling class selection and prev/next handling beyond delegation and callback refresh.
Mutex ownership sampling and waiter management beyond wait protection usage.
Pressure group hierarchy organization and periodic aggregation details beyond self-wake suppression.
Extended scheduler emptiness checks and high-resolution tick interactions.
Balance callback lifecycle and run queue pinning rules beyond clearing before unlock.
Clock flag meanings and clock update effects beyond promotion and refresh.

findings.text: Scheduling mode codes distinguish four request types with fixed numeric values: idle uses negative one, none uses zero, preemption uses one, and RT lock waiting uses two. Callers pass one of these values into the central scheduling routine to select sleep versus preemption handling.

Voluntary scheduling is entered through a globally visible routine that can be invoked from task context. It records worker sleep state when the caller is not runnable, repeatedly invokes the central switch logic while rescheduling is requested, and then records worker running state.

Terminal task exit is entered through a non-returning routine that marks the current execution context as dead and exempt from freezing, invokes the central switch logic once in non-preemptive mode, and then parks in a relaxed spin if control unexpectedly returns.

Pressure stall accounting exposes a switch hook that observes previous and next execution contexts plus a sleep indicator. It updates per-CPU write state and propagates running and waiting indications through the associated hierarchy.

Proxy execution exposes a resolution helper that, given a run queue and a blocked donor candidate, determines the runnable owner that should execute on behalf of the chain. One build variant performs chain walking while the other only warns and returns its input.

Core-aware stealing preserves grouping affinity by requiring an active grouping identifier on the destination shared structure and an idle destination. Only a queued member of that grouping may move, excluding the source current and current selection, requiring destination eligibility, bounded occupation relative to idle, and absence of throttling on both sides.

Balancing scans scheduling domains in hierarchical order and candidate peers in wrapped order starting after the local processor. The scan stops early when rescheduling becomes necessary or when one relocation succeeds, ensuring at most one successful move per invocation.

Sibling processors sharing simultaneous multithreading share one leader structure. A solitary sibling remains self-led. Joining installs the existing leader across all siblings, leaving validates the leader and otherwise transfers shared sequencing and grouping state to a successor while moving in-flight accounting to avoid permanent bias.

Blocking state combines a persistent blocked indicator with an optional mutex association. A pending signal clears the association and forces runnable status without dequeuing. Otherwise the indicator is set, and dequeuing occurs only when the caller requests actual blocking, allowing mutex-blocked tasks to remain selectable for proxy execution.

Proxy bookkeeping maintains a donor pointer per run queue that is refreshed on every selection and cleared of donor linkage on the chosen candidate. When the donor identity survives across a switch involving different tasks, class callbacks are re-invoked to avoid missing balancing opportunities for the outgoing task.

Cookie relocation holds interrupt protection together with ordered acquisition of both involved run queue locks for the whole search and move. This prevents concurrent selection or migration on either queue while eligibility is evaluated and while the queued task is transferred.

Core balancing is entered with the local run queue lock held but releases it across the domain scan under preemption and read-copy-update protection, then reacquires it before returning. Hotplug joining and leaving serialize leader installation and state transfer under a dedicated core guard keyed by the affected processor.

Chain resolution for proxy execution acquires the mutex wait protection and the per-task blocked protection while validating the association and sampling the owner. Stability of the association under both protections is required to proceed; any observed change forces a retry by the outer scheduling loop rather than acting on stale linkage.

Proxy migration and temporary unlocking clear pending balancing callbacks before dropping run queue protection to avoid pinning violations if another processor balances concurrently. After cross-queue attachment completes, protection is reacquired with clock refresh, and the caller forces a fresh selection so callbacks are re-established.

Each run queue carries core-scheduling shared state reachable through a core pointer, including grouping identifier, sequencing counters for tasks and selections, in-flight selection count, and forced-idle accounting with count, sequence and occupation plus start time. Per-processor balancing state includes a dedicated callback head.

Task state relevant to proxying includes a blocked indicator, an associated mutex pointer protected by a dedicated lock, a donor linkage used while resolving chains, a preserved wake processor across forced placement, and queue membership plus delayed-dequeue and throttling indications consulted during selection and migration.

Context switching consults and updates run queue counters for switches, current and donor pointers, next scheduling class, clock update flags and rescheduling timestamps, plus per-task voluntary and involuntary switch counts, state word, scheduling class operations, and pressure stall flags for running, waiting and on-processor indications.

The central switch routine interprets its mode to choose accounting and blocking behavior. Idle mode allows a fast path when no runnable work exists and extended scheduling is disabled. Preemptive mode treats the caller as runnable and counts a preemption, while non-preemptive modes with a non-zero state attempt blocking and count a voluntary switch.

Core leadership follows a small lifecycle: solitary operation is self-led, activation discovers and adopts the surviving leader, deactivation of a leader elects a successor and transfers shared state with reset of transient forced-idle timing, and the dying stage severs non-leader linkage back to self.

Proxy resolution yields one of several outcomes: run the current task when waking is observed, run the terminal owner when fully local and queued, schedule idle to allow concurrent wakeup or migration to complete, deactivate the examined task when its owner is absent or not runnable, migrate it toward a remote owner, or request a fresh selection on races.

Outer scheduling forms a loop that disables preemption, performs one central switch, re-enables preemption without rescheduling, and repeats while a rescheduling request remains pending, ensuring coalesced requests are drained before returning to task context.

Deactivating or migrating a donor while run queue references still point at it would allow a concurrent wakeup on another processor to reuse freed linkage. The implementation therefore switches the queue to idle and updates donor and class state before dequeuing, ensuring no stale pointers survive the lock drop.

Testing for pending signals after acquiring run queue protection, combined with a full ordering barrier, prevents lost wakeups between the caller marking sleep and a concurrent signal delivery. If a signal is present the task is forced runnable and its blocked association is cleared instead of sleeping.

Owners may move between processors or change queue state while a chain is examined. The code mitigates this by revalidating queue membership and processor identity after sampling, treating migrating or remote owners as reasons to idle or relocate rather than dereference, and by handling a self-owner interleaving with unlock as an idle decision.

Pressure accounting normally wakes periodic aggregation when task state changes after quiescence, but doing so when the outgoing task is the aggregation worker itself would cause indefinite self-wake ping-pong. That specific case suppresses the wake while other sleeps still trigger it.

Pressure updates avoid duplicate hierarchy walks by marking the incoming hierarchy up to the first already-marked ancestor shared with the outgoing task, then applying outgoing changes only below that point and propagating residual flag differences above it.

Sleep preparation establishes a non-blocking validation context, notifies the appropriate worker subsystem for workqueue or IO workers, asserts absence of RT lock waiting, flushes any plugged IO, and then releases the validation context. Wakeup performs the complementary running notification.
In the observed build variant, next-task selection is a thin delegation to the shared selection helper while retaining the requirement that the run queue lock is held across the call.

Pressure reporting on context switch is conditional on a global disabled indicator in one build, delegating to full accounting only when enabled, while the alternate build provides an empty operation that performs no work.
